title: Scaling Agentic AI Factories Through Extreme Co-Design with NVIDIA BlueField
event_hint: NVIDIA BlueField-4 / Vera BlueField-4 STX + DOCA platform positioning for agentic AI factory data-path offload (context-memory via DOCA Memos).
problem: Agentic inference extends beyond model execution into a distributed workflow of tool calls, retrieval, KV-cache persistence, policy checks, storage and network transfers; infrastructure services running on host CPUs contend with agent execution inside the reasoning loop and can stall tool execution, retrieval and validation even when GPU compute is available, while GPU memory pressure forces KV-cache eviction, recompute or context-length limits that trade latency, throughput and cost.
mechanism: BlueField-4 DPU (up to 800 Gb/s Ethernet/InfiniBand, 64-core Grace CPU, LPDDR5X, PCIe Gen6) and the Vera BlueField-4 STX Storage Processor (Vera CPU + ConnectX-9 + up to 1.6 Tb/s Spectrum-X) run networking, storage, security, telemetry and control-plane services in a dedicated in-silicon domain outside the host. DOCA exposes these as programmable services: DOCA HBN (server-side L3/BGP on BlueField), BlueField ASTRA (Spectrum-X zero-trust multi-tenant bare-metal control point with ConnectX-9), DOCA Memos (cross-node KV-cache management/sharing), and DOCA security services (zero-trust access, policy, runtime visibility, isolation). The STX storage processor runs KV I/O, KV-metadata tracking, queue management, cache recall/pre-staging and tenant policy close to the storage/network path instead of presenting flash as block storage, powering the NVIDIA CMX context-memory tier between GPU memory and shared storage.

evidence.claim: BlueField-4 integrates up to 800 Gb/s Ethernet or InfiniBand, a 64-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, high-bandwidth LPDDR5X memory, PCIe Gen6, inline acceleration and the DOCA software platform.
evidence.value: up to 800 Gb/s; 64-core Grace CPU; PCIe Gen6; LPDDR5X
evidence.condition: BlueField-4 DPU specifications, Vera Rubin platform
evidence.source_locator: Section: BlueField powers the operating system of the AI factory

evidence.claim: Compared with BlueField-3, BlueField-4 doubles networking bandwidth, delivers up to 6x more compute performance, 4x memory capacity and more than 3x memory bandwidth.
evidence.value: 2x networking bandwidth; up to 6x compute; 4x memory capacity; >3x memory bandwidth
evidence.condition: BlueField-4 vs BlueField-3 (architectural comparison, no workload defined)
evidence.source_locator: Section: BlueField powers the operating system of the AI factory

evidence.claim: The Vera BlueField-4 STX Storage Processor combines the NVIDIA Vera CPU, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, up to 1.6 Tb/s Spectrum-X Ethernet, NVMe storage access, accelerated data movement, in-silicon security and DOCA programmability.
evidence.value: up to 1.6 Tb/s Spectrum-X; ConnectX-9; Vera CPU
evidence.source_locator: Section: BlueField powers the operating system of the AI factory

evidence.claim: DOCA Memos manages and shares KV cache across compute and storage nodes so context can be reused across long-context and agentic inference; KV-cache reuse reduces repeated prefill, context recomputation, GPU idle time and unnecessary data movement.
evidence.value: KV-cache reuse across compute and CMX data nodes
evidence.baseline: recompute/eviction of KV cache on GPU memory pressure
evidence.condition: long-context and agentic workloads via DOCA Memos + NVIDIA CMX context-memory tier
evidence.source_locator: Section: System-level capabilities of BlueField; Section: AI-native storage and context memory

evidence.claim: BlueField-4 operates as the infrastructure processor in the GPU compute tray for frontend (north-south) networking, host CPU offload, secure data access, management, observability and isolation, with higher frontend bandwidth and lower host CPU contention claimed to support more predictable inference latency and higher tokens per second per user.
evidence.value: more predictable inference latency; higher tokens per second per user (directional, no magnitude)
evidence.condition: directional benefit stated without a quantified benchmark
evidence.source_locator: Section: GPU compute: Securing and accelerating Rubin GPUs

evaluation_context: NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform co-design: Rubin GPUs, Vera CPUs, NVLink scale-up, ConnectX-9 + Spectrum-X scale-out, BlueField-4 DPU, Vera BlueField-4 STX storage processor, NVIDIA CMX context-memory tier, DOCA software. Target workload is agentic AI factories (multi-turn agents, long-context reasoning, RAG, multi-agent). The evidence is architectural/positioning prose; no benchmark table, hardware configuration, measured latency/throughput/CPU-utilization numbers, or baseline workload are disclosed in the visible Evidence Pack.
limitations: This is a vendor technical blog, not a measurement paper. The Evidence Pack exposes only architectural claims and directional benefits (higher GPU utilization, more predictable latency, lower cost per token, more tokens per watt, 2x/6x/4x/3x vs BlueField-3) with no workload-defined benchmark, no measured CPU-offload percentage, no end-to-end latency or throughput figures, and no deployment scale. The 6x/4x/3x comparisons are silicon-spec ratios versus BlueField-3, not agentic-workload results. Quantitative validation of KV-cache-reuse gain (tokens per second, power efficiency) is asserted but not measured in the visible text.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to the DPU inline-offload topic: BlueField-4 + DOCA Memos is a concrete instance of moving KV-cache management, storage metadata, security, telemetry and control-plane services into the DPU/storage-processor in-path domain rather than the host CPU, which is the project's core question of which data-path operations can run inline on a DPU and whether single-point offload can form an end-to-end gain. The CMX + DOCA Memos path is the most project-relevant抓手 for cross-domain KV-cache/context-memory offload; the next verification step is finding any measured CPU-offload, latency or tokens-per-second/watt numbers for agentic workloads under this stack.

evidence_gaps.question: Are there measured quantitative results for agentic workloads (CPU-offload percentage, end-to-end latency, tokens per second, tokens per watt, KV-cache reuse hit rate) on the BlueField-4 + DOCA Memos stack?
What is the concrete deployment scale or configuration for the claimed BlueField-4 gains inside a Vera Rubin AI factory?
